title: Mensuration and geometry
syllabus: Areas and volumes of plane figures and solids
summary: Use the stated formulas for a rectangle, a triangle, a circle, a cylinder, a sphere, and a cube, keep the units straight, and add the volumes of a cylinder and a hemisphere.
intuition:
Mensuration questions are a match between a shape and a formula you have already written down. This lesson uses a rectangle of length $l$ and width $w$, with area $lw$ and perimeter $2(l+w)$; a triangle, with area $\tfrac12 ab\sin C$ and also Heron's formula once the semi-perimeter $s=(a+b+c)/2$ is defined; a circle, with area $\pi r^2$ and circumference $2\pi r$; a cylinder, with volume $\pi r^2 h$ and curved surface area $2\pi r h$; a sphere, with volume $\tfrac43\pi r^3$ and surface area $4\pi r^2$; and a cube of side $a$, with volume $a^3$ and surface area $6a^2$. A right angle also brings Pythagoras: if the legs are $a$ and $b$ and the hypotenuse is $c$, then $a^2+b^2=c^2$.

Units travel with the quantity. Lengths add to a length. An area is in square centimetres. A volume is in cubic centimetres. Multiplying three lengths produces a volume, and it does not produce an area.

A solid made of two pieces has the volume of the first piece plus the volume of the second, provided you do not count the shared face as a third solid. The worked solid is a cylinder with a hemisphere of the same radius on one end. The hemisphere is half a sphere, so its volume is half of $\tfrac43\pi r^3$, which is $\tfrac23\pi r^3$. That half is stated here because it is used. No formula is used before it is stated.

definitions.body: For a triangle with sides $a$, $b$, and $c$, $s=(a+b+c)/2$. Heron's formula is $\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$.
The lateral area $2\pi r h$, not including the two circular ends. The volume $\pi r^2 h$ is a different quantity.
A hemisphere of radius $r$ has volume half of $\tfrac43\pi r^3$, that is $\tfrac23\pi r^3$. The sphere formulas are $V=\tfrac43\pi r^3$ and $S=4\pi r^2$.
A triangle with a right angle. The legs $a$ and $b$ and hypotenuse $c$ satisfy $a^2+b^2=c^2$, and the area is $\tfrac12 ab$.

formulas.name: Triangle
formulas.note: $s=(a+b+c)/2$. For a right angle between sides $a$ and $b$, $\sin C=1$ and the area is $\tfrac12 ab$.

formulas.name: Circle and sphere
formulas.latex: A=\pi r^2,\ C=2\pi r,\quad V=\tfrac43\pi r^3,\ S=4\pi r^2
formulas.note: The sphere surface is $4\pi r^2$. The factor $\tfrac43\pi r^3$ is the volume, not the surface.

formulas.name: Cylinder
formulas.latex: V=\pi r^2 h,\quad \text{curved area}=2\pi r h
formulas.note: Curved area excludes the two bases.

formulas.name: Rectangle, cube, Pythagoras
formulas.note: Rectangle area and perimeter, cube volume and surface area, then the right-triangle relation.

properties: Area is measured in square units and volume in cubic units. A radius in centimetres gives an area in $\text{cm}^2$ and a volume in $\text{cm}^3$.
For sides 8, 15, and 17, $8^2+15^2=64+225=289=17^2$, so the triangle is right-angled and the area is $\tfrac12\times 8\times 15=60$.
Heron's formula on the same triangle, with $s=20$, returns $\sqrt{20\times 3\times 5\times 12}=\sqrt{3600}=60$. The two area formulas agree.
A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm has volume $36\pi\ \text{cm}^3$ and curved surface $24\pi\ \text{cm}^2$.
Half of the sphere volume $\tfrac43\pi r^3$ at $r=3$ is $18\pi$. Adding that hemisphere to the cylinder gives $36\pi+18\pi=54\pi\ \text{cm}^3$.

examples.title: The same triangle by Pythagoras and by Heron
examples.prompt: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 15 cm, and 17 cm. Show that it is right-angled, and find its area in two ways. Also record the area and perimeter of a 12 cm by 5 cm rectangle, for the unit contrast.
steps: Check Pythagoras: $8^2+15^2=64+225=289=17^2$. The angle between the sides of 8 cm and 15 cm is a right angle, so one area formula gives $\tfrac12\times 8\times 15=60\ \text{cm}^2$.
The semi-perimeter is $(8+15+17)/2=20$. Heron's formula gives $\sqrt{20(20-17)(20-15)(20-8)}=\sqrt{20\times 3\times 5\times 12}=\sqrt{3600}=60\ \text{cm}^2$.
The rectangle has area $12\times 5=60\ \text{cm}^2$ and perimeter $2(12+5)=34$ cm. Same number of area units as the triangle, different shape, and the perimeter is a length, not an area.
examples.answer: The triangle is right-angled with area $60\ \text{cm}^2$ by both formulas. The rectangle has area $60\ \text{cm}^2$ and perimeter 34 cm.

examples.title: A cylinder with a hemisphere on one end
examples.prompt: A solid is a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm attached at one end. Find the volume. Also state the cube of side 5 cm for comparison.
steps: The cylinder volume is $\pi r^2 h=\pi\times 9\times 4=36\pi\ \text{cm}^3$.
The sphere of radius 3 cm has volume $\tfrac43\pi\times 27=36\pi\ \text{cm}^3$. The hemisphere is half of that, $18\pi\ \text{cm}^3$.

The solid's volume is $36\pi+18\pi=54\pi\ \text{cm}^3$. A cube of side 5 cm has volume $5^3=125\ \text{cm}^3$ and surface area $6\times 25=150\ \text{cm}^2$, which are not multiples of $\pi$ because the cube is not round.
examples.answer: The combined volume is $54\pi\ \text{cm}^3$. The cube has volume $125\ \text{cm}^3$.

traps: Using $\tfrac43\pi r^3$ as the surface area of a sphere. That is the volume. The surface area is $4\pi r^2$.
Calling $2\pi r h$ the volume of a cylinder. That is the curved surface. The volume is $\pi r^2 h$.
Adding a hemisphere of radius 3 cm as a full sphere, which would give $36\pi+36\pi=72\pi$ instead of $54\pi$.
Reporting an area in cm or a volume in $\text{cm}^2$. The rectangle perimeter is 34 cm; its area is $60\ \text{cm}^2$.
python:
assert 12 * 5 == 60
assert 2 * (12 + 5) == 34
assert 8 ** 2 + 15 ** 2 == 17 ** 2 == 289
s = (8 + 15 + 17) // 2
assert s == 20
heron_sq = s * (s - 17) * (s - 15) * (s - 8)
assert heron_sq == 3600
assert heron_sq ** 0.5 == 60
assert (8 * 15) // 2 == 60
assert 3 ** 2 * 4 == 36
assert 2 * 3 * 4 == 24
sphere_coeff = (4 * 3 ** 3) // 3
assert sphere_coeff == 36
hemi = sphere_coeff // 2
assert hemi == 18
assert 36 + 18 == 54
assert 5 ** 3 == 125
assert 6 * 5 ** 2 == 150
print(54)

questions.stem: A triangle has sides 8 cm, 15 cm, and 17 cm, and $8^2+15^2=17^2$. Its area is
questions.solution: The answer is **A**, $60\ \text{cm}^2$. The right angle gives $\tfrac12\times 8\times 15=60$. Heron agrees: $s=20$ and $\sqrt{20\times 3\times 5\times 12}=\sqrt{3600}=60$. Option B is the product $8\times 15$ without the factor $\tfrac12$.

questions.stem: A cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm has a hemisphere of the same radius attached at one end. The volume of the solid is
questions.solution: The answer is **A**, $54\pi\ \text{cm}^3$. The cylinder is $\pi r^2 h=36\pi$. The full sphere is $\tfrac43\pi r^3=36\pi$, so the hemisphere is $18\pi$. The sum is $54\pi$. Option B is the cylinder alone, and option D is what you would get by adding a full sphere.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 12 cm by 5 cm, and a cube has side 5 cm. A sphere has radius $r$. Which of the following are true?
options: The surface area of the sphere is $\tfrac43\pi r^3$.
questions.solution: The correct options are **A, B, and C**. The rectangle area is $12\times 5=60\ \text{cm}^2$ and the perimeter is $2(12+5)=34$ cm. The cube volume is $5^3=125\ \text{cm}^3$. Option D quotes the sphere volume formula as if it were the surface area. The surface area is $4\pi r^2$.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 8 cm and 15 cm. Enter the hypotenuse in centimetres.
questions.solution: The answer is **17**. Pythagoras gives $c^2=8^2+15^2=64+225=289$, and $c=\sqrt{289}=17$ since a length is positive. The area $60$ is not the hypotenuse.

questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Its curved surface area, excluding the two bases, is
questions.solution: The answer is **A**, $24\pi\ \text{cm}^2$. The curved area is $2\pi r h=2\pi\times 3\times 4=24\pi$. Option B, $36\pi$, is the volume coefficient $\pi r^2 h$, which is a volume in $\text{cm}^3$, not the curved area.
